summary: Added a soak harness that generates real load through the real ExecutionSupervisor over a durable TaskLedger, Scheduler, RecoveryScheduler and CircuitBreaker, samples eleven resource and health dimensions continuously, and gates its verdict on the tier's own duration AND every measured invariant. The 30-minute tier was actually run to completion on this host. The 2h, 8h and overnight tiers are implemented and selectable but were NOT executed in this round, and are therefore reported as not-run rather than as passes, per the taskbook.
implementation: src/shared/soak-harness.ts (pure): SOAK_TIER_SPECS with smoke/30m/2h/8h/overnight and a per-tier audit bar (a tier that only ran its first minutes has not demonstrated anything); SoakSample covering RSS, heapUsed, external memory, handles, requests, CPU time, completed/failed/retries, queue depth, open circuits, provider failures, stale sessions, live child processes, renderer health (optional, so its absence is explicit) and the process id; eleven invariants (duration-reached, no-unexpected-restart, rss-bounded, heap-bounded, handles-bounded, queue-drained, failure-ratio-bounded, throughput-above-floor, no-stale-sessions, no-orphan-processes, provider-crash-loop-bounded) with declared SOAK_BOUNDS; evaluateSoakInvariants; soakVerdict returning PASS only when the duration was completed AND every invariant holds, otherwise BLOCKED_EXTERNAL (host could not sustain it) or INCOMPLETE_WITH_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE (stopped early); renderSoakReport

electron/host/soak-harness.ts: real durable machinery in the run's own directory; two synthetic runtimes with a periodic injected retryable timeout; continuous sampling on a fixed interval; a heartbeat written after every sample so a killed run keeps the evidence it earned (and a resume from a prior heartbeat is recorded as a restart); bounded real child-process pool; awaited cleanup that escalates to taskkill and waits on the real exit event, with the post-cleanup survivor count recorded as the orphan measurement

used as the harness self-check; a 20s run with real load, real child processes and cleanup, which is what exercised the two cleanup defects below.

defects_found_by_this_evidence: the harness spawned one real child process per task with no ceiling. The orphan invariant failed immediately on the first smoke run and was right: a soak that forks per unit of work is itself the leak. It now runs a fixed, bounded pool

the first orphan check conflated the live worker pool with a leak, and polling exitCode after kill() reported a mid-exit process as an orphan because that field only advances on the real exit event. Cleanup now escalates to taskkill /T /F and awaits the event; the pool is reported as an informational resource reading and only post-cleanup survivors count against the invariant
tests: tests/unit/host-soak-harness.test.ts (30 tests): the four plan tiers plus the smoke self-check with their audit bars, and an unknown tier rejected rather than defaulted; a healthy run passes and every invariant in it is asserted individually 鈥?the live child pool is not counted as an orphan, a survivor after cleanup fails, an unobserved cleanup is UNAVAILABLE, an unreached duration fails, an unexpected restart fails, and each of heap/RSS/handle growth fails only beyond its declared bound; the queue invariant fails when the backlog is still present in the tail window and passes when the tail shows it draining; failures dominating settled work fail; a run too short to measure throughput reports UNAVAILABLE rather than FAIL; stale sessions and a provider crash loop fail; fewer than two samples reports the trend invariants UNAVAILABLE; an interrupted run is never PASS and a blocked host is never PASS; a breach fails even when the duration was reached; summary and rendering expose every observed value and bound. Runs: a bounded tier samples real resources and writes a heartbeat; renderer health is declared UNAVAILABLE with a reason and never faked; the child pool is real, observed during the run and gone after cleanup; an injected retry is recorded rather than hidden; every artefact lands inside the run's own directory; and a prior heartbeat is detected as a resume
